state_meaning: AI-drafted candidate; no person has reviewed it.
text: The authors describe wanting an agent to maximize a complex objective such as how happy a user would be after spending hours inspecting the result, while lacking time to provide such oversight for every training example, so training relies on cheaper proxies (does the user seem happy, is there visible dirt) that do not perfectly track what we care about. They say this divergence worsens side effects and reward hacking, and that it may be eased by using a limited oversight budget more efficiently, e.g. combining limited calls to the true objective with frequent calls to an imperfect given or learned proxy.
title: Scalable oversight problem: expensive true objective vs cheap imperfect proxies
